newsitem.title: CHILE: Rainstorm whips Chile, four killed and 2,000 homeless.
newsitem.headline: Rainstorm whips Chile, four killed and 2,000 homeless.

text.p: More than 2,000 people were forced from their homes, at least four were killed and neighbourhoods were flooded when a severe rainstorm whipped Chile on Wednesday, authorities said.
The storm, which ended a year-long drought in much of the country, tore off roofs and caused flash floods in parts of Santiago and as far south as the city of Puerto Montt, they said.
In the northern desert city of La Serena the storm brought the first rain in four years, and in the southern city of Concepcion the wind uprooted big, centuries-old trees in the main square.
The deaths included a couple killed when a rain-sodden wall collapsed on them in the town of Los Angeles and a policeman crushed when a tree fell on the squad car he was driving.

Rescuers found the body of a fisherman on a beach near Concepcion after winds and waves overturned his small boat. Up to six other men believed to have been aboard were missing and may be drowned, state television reported.
A large Chilean-flagged fishing trawler, the Zuderser, capsized in heavy surf as it was docked in the southern port of Talcahuano.
Streets and parks in low-lying parts of Santiago were under water Tuesday night and early Wednesday, causing traffic jams.

In some areas, the storm brought the first significant rainfall since a drought began afflicting central Chile in mid-1996, triggering water rationing. Rainfall levels in Santiago were slightly above normal for the year after the downpour, the national meteorological service said.
Most of the 2,000 evacuees were from low-lying slums along the banks of the Bio Bio river near Concepcion, where the storm hit hardest after it blew in off Pacific, the service said.
